entry_points: main() via require.main and CLI argv; --plan plus registered --apply/--rollback/--verify/--seed commands
reads: all migration/rollback/verify/seed paths registered in FILES
writes: executes substituted SQL through EWOH_DATABASE_URL/SUDA_DATABASE_URL in one transaction per command
database_tables: all tables addressed by registered legacy/standalone migrations, verifies and seeds
contracts: destructive gate only for commands in stale ROLLBACK_COMMANDS
security_boundaries: schema regex validation and derived role names
admin username whitelist, bcrypt cost 12, 12+ password, literal escaping
tenant_boundaries: standalone forces public
legacy uses validated EWOH_SCHEMA or workspace default

SQL errors exit 1 and close connection
newer rollback commands can bypass destructive gate

findings.evidence: ROLLBACK_COMMANDS ends at 057 while rollback commands for 058+ are registered but absent from the set checked by the destructive gate.
findings.impact: Direct runner rollback of newer migrations requires only the DDL flag, bypassing intended destructive authorization; standalone-chain separately gates whole-chain rollback.
findings.fix: Derive gated rollback commands from the dispatch map or register every rollback command and add a completeness regression test.

findings.evidence: No applied-version ledger exists; execution relies on idempotent files and one transaction per command.
findings.impact: Partial state is not explicit and apply does not automatically prove success; recovery depends on every migration being re-entrant.
findings.fix: Persist ordered migration receipts and run paired verification immediately or atomically with apply.

findings.evidence: Simple verify searches all result rows for the first object containing the assertion field.
findings.impact: Unexpected result cardinality or duplicate fields can be masked when one value equals 1.
findings.fix: Assert expected result-set/row cardinality and unique assertion fields.

findings.evidence: Core-table reconciliation extracts names from the first line after a fixed SQL marker.
findings.impact: Formatting changes fail closed; equivalent alternate SQL could evade extraction.
findings.fix: Generate both expected lists from structured metadata or use deterministic parsing.

semantic_analysis.migration_safety: Each execute command runs substituted SQL in one transaction; standalone-chain adds ordering, but the runner itself has no schema-state receipt or automatic post-apply verify.
semantic_analysis.replay_safety: Replay depends entirely on re-entrant SQL; direct replay of an older migration can regress newer policy state.
semantic_analysis.owner_runtime_roles: No runtime connection switch here; SQL may create roles and inject validated/escaped credentials.
semantic_analysis.schema_alignment: Core verify is manifest-driven and explicit; targeted verifies often hard-code counts in handlers.
semantic_analysis.injection_risk: Schema is regex validated; credentials and seed identity strings are escaped. No untrusted runtime parameters are directly interpolated.
semantic_analysis.verification_guarantees: Guarantees are command-scoped and mixed: manifest reconciliation, single-field assertions, or handler count assertions; no universal behavioral RLS probe.

entry_points: runChain() via require.main and one --apply/--verify/--rollback/--plan CLI argument
writes: spawns run_migrations.js per migration with inherited stdio/environment
contracts: DFS apply and reverse rollback order
tenant_boundaries: delegates to standalone runner, forcing public
failure_paths: child spawn error/nonzero status stops chain

findings.evidence: Each migration is a separate child transaction and chain failure stops immediately without a persisted step receipt or per-step verify.
findings.impact: Interruptions leave partial state and recovery depends on complete replay idempotency.
findings.fix: Persist step receipts or automatically verify each step and make resume semantics explicit.

findings.evidence: Plan validates EXECUTE_COMMANDS and rollback keys but cannot inspect the private command-to-file map.
findings.impact: A plan can pass while an apply/rollback later fails at read(undefined) if mappings drift; current data passes.
findings.fix: Export and cross-check the dispatch map or centralize command registration.

findings.evidence: spawnSync has no timeout.
findings.impact: A hung migration child blocks the chain indefinitely.
findings.fix: Define timeout/cancellation behavior and ensure connections close.

semantic_analysis.migration_safety: Strong static ordering, disk registration, dependency cycle and rollback-registration checks; no global transaction or chain receipt.
semantic_analysis.replay_safety: Always replays all migrations in dependency order; rollback reverses completed DFS order.
semantic_analysis.rls_org_isolation: Dependent entirely on migration SQL and verifies.
semantic_analysis.injection_risk: No shell and no untrusted interpolation.
semantic_analysis.verification_guarantees: --verify stops on first failed migration verify; --apply performs no automatic verification.

entry_points: main() at module load; operator provisioning/maintenance CLI
writes: INSERT/UPDATE ewoh_user identity, credentials, org, roles, status and person binding
contracts: existing accounts unchanged unless explicit flags
security_boundaries: owner rather than business runtime role required
tenant_boundaries: schema and organization explicitly selected
default org is arbitrary first row when omitted
owner list intentionally bypasses RLS

findings.evidence: Password, roles, person and status maintenance updates run as independent statements without a transaction.
findings.impact: Mid-command failure can leave credentials, authorization, binding or status inconsistent.
findings.fix: Wrap maintenance updates in sql.begin and report one committed outcome.

findings.evidence: Without --org-id it chooses ORDER BY id LIMIT 1 across all organizations.
findings.impact: Multi-org deployments can silently bind an operator to the wrong tenant.
findings.fix: Require explicit org when multiple organizations exist or resolve an explicitly supplied slug/name.

findings.evidence: A pre-check is followed by INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and unconditional created output.
findings.impact: Concurrent creation can be silently ignored yet reported as created with requested values not applied.
findings.fix: Use atomic upsert/RETURNING or inspect affected rows.

findings.evidence: Documented mutually exclusive password sources are not actually mutually exclusive; stdin silently wins.
findings.impact: Operators may think an explicit env password was used.
findings.fix: Reject conflicting sources and validate the custom env variable name.

semantic_analysis.migration_safety: Operational identity provisioning, not schema migration; existing account behavior is conservative.
semantic_analysis.idempotency: No-flag rerun is no-op and insert is conflict-protected, but reporting is not race-correct.
semantic_analysis.owner_runtime_roles: Correctly requires owner access for ewoh_user while runtime identity access is constrained elsewhere.
semantic_analysis.schema_alignment: Matches user/person binding concepts; role list is duplicated rather than imported from a shared contract.
semantic_analysis.injection_risk: Schema is validated and all mutable values parameterized/sql.json encoded.
semantic_analysis.verification_guarantees: No RETURNING/affected-row receipt or post-write verification.

migration chain is database source of truth
drizzle-kit push not used for production

org columns represented for RLS-protected tables
Drizzle parameters are generated by ORM when used

baseline UUID org tables and legacy varchar tables coexist

findings.evidence: The file explicitly acknowledges ai_suggestion/production_task/schedule_task varchar mappings drift from standalone_001 UUID columns.
findings.impact: TS accepts values PostgreSQL rejects, joins/casts can behave differently across tables, and drizzle-kit can infer unintended type changes despite the no-push rule.
findings.fix: Create an ADR-backed type convergence or generated dual-type mapping, then add an automated migration/schema contract check.

findings.evidence: Standalone_061/068 org+time/covering indexes are not represented on ewoh_telemetry and ewoh_device, while some ewoh_event org indexes are represented.
findings.impact: Schema introspection/push and code readers do not see the deployed query path; accidental regeneration can drop performance-critical indexes.
findings.fix: Add migration-aligned index declarations with SQL include/partial semantics or generate schema mappings from a structured migration contract.

findings.evidence: The task/snapshot unique index lacks org_id even though route matrix rows are org-scoped and 057 only compounds matrix_id.
findings.impact: Two tenants using the same task/snapshot key cannot both cache rows despite RLS isolation; one tenant can cause the other insert/write to fail.
findings.fix: Compound the logical full key with org_id (or generate globally unique task keys) and align migration, schema and verify.

findings.evidence: reservation_id remains globally unique while resource reservations are org-scoped.
findings.impact: Cross-tenant reservation ID reuse is rejected even though RLS should make tenants independent.
findings.fix: Use (org_id,reservation_id) uniqueness and update lookup/upsert behavior atomically.

findings.evidence: fromDriver parses composite/array strings by slicing and splitting on commas without PostgreSQL composite quoting rules.
findings.impact: A comma-bearing bucket/path or profile component can round-trip as corrupt fields even after safe SQL literal escaping.
findings.fix: Use the PostgreSQL composite parser/driver parser or define IDs/paths that exclude delimiters and enforce both write and read validation.

findings.evidence: Standalone_098 sets a GUC/default-org column DEFAULT, but the Drizzle orgId field has no default.
findings.impact: Drizzle introspection/push sees a default mismatch and new ORM inserts omit the deployed DB default semantics.
findings.fix: Represent the SQL default exactly or make inserts explicitly org-aware and prevent push.

findings.evidence: The closing unmapclaimed-table note says ewoh_device_capability has no mapping although it is mapped above.
findings.impact: Maintainers may duplicate or remove the mapping based on contradictory guidance.
findings.fix: Remove ewoh_device_capability from the stale exclusion list and automate mapping-note consistency.

semantic_analysis.module_shape: Declarative Drizzle metadata only; no direct SQL execution or event side effects.
semantic_analysis.schema_alignment: Mostly detailed and migration-annotated, but known type drift, absent newer indexes, DB-only defaults and several global business keys prevent an exact current-state mapping.
semantic_analysis.owner_runtime_roles: No role logic; RLS behavior is inferred only from comments/columns.
semantic_analysis.injection_risk: escapeLiteral is intentionally conservative but does not make composite output parsing fully structured.
semantic_analysis.verification_guarantees: No standalone test proves the full TypeScript mapping equals migration state; verification is distributed through service and RLS tests.

contracts: org equality using current GUC with legacy fallback

no migration-state ledger in SQL itself

findings.evidence: Every policy contains USING/WITH CHECK `OR org_id IS NULL`. Standalone_057 later removes these branches, but direct replay of this older command restores them.
findings.impact: A direct idempotent rerun temporarily or persistently downgrades eight production tenant policies and again allows global NULL rows if constraints change; full-chain replay repairs it only because 057 runs later.
findings.fix: Mark this migration as superseded/prohibit out-of-order direct replay, or make old migrations forward-safe by incorporating the final 057 policy shape.

findings.evidence: Verification counts RLS flags, named policies, textual GUC references and column existence but does not run org-A/org-B/fail-closed row probes.
findings.impact: A semantically wrong but textually similar policy or lost grant can pass structural verification.
findings.fix: Use role-switched behavioral probes like standalone_098 and assert grants/constraints.

findings.evidence: Comments and column comment describe NULL as global, which standalone_057 intentionally supersedes with NOT NULL/fail-closed behavior.
findings.impact: Replay/audit readers can mistake the transient contract for the final tenant contract.
findings.fix: Add a visible superseded-by annotation and update comments during a forward-safe revision.

semantic_analysis.migration_safety: All operations are conditional or DROP/CREATE and execute in one runner transaction; safe as the original step and fresh-chain replay.
semantic_analysis.replay_safety: Not forward-safe after 057: direct replay restores the older fail-open NULL branch.
semantic_analysis.owner_runtime_roles: Policies target service_role; no role switch inside migration.
semantic_analysis.schema_alignment: Adds nullable varchar org_id matching the pre-057 state; current chain later makes it NOT NULL.
semantic_analysis.injection_risk: Schema token is runner-validated; policy expressions are static.
semantic_analysis.verification_guarantees: Structural existence/GUC text only, not actual isolation behavior.

entry_points: applied by run_migrations.js --apply-standalone-rls-null-reject; paired rollback command
writes: backfills org_id and sets NOT NULL on 15 scheduler/route/policy tables
adds snapshot lineage and reservation org index
contracts: NOT NULL org_id after default-org backfill
security_boundaries: policies restricted to service_role except authenticated knowledge SELECT
tenant_boundaries: exact org text equality with legacy GUC fallback
NULL no longer permitted on 15 tables
world snapshots/assignment events/outbox/prediction observations explicitly remain global/shared or derived
failure_paths: missing tables/columns or duplicate business keys abort transaction

findings.evidence: Legacy NULL rows are backfilled to lexicographically min(org_id::text), or a hardcoded sentinel when no organization exists.
findings.impact: In an existing multi-org database, orphan/global rows can be silently assigned to an arbitrary tenant, changing visibility and ownership.
findings.fix: Use an explicit migration parameter/approved default tenant, or quarantine ambiguous rows and require operator mapping before NOT NULL.

findings.evidence: Verification checks policy role/text absence of the literal NULL branch, workbench policy names and index names, but not full policy semantics, workbench RLS flags, org idempotency index or behavior.
findings.impact: Equivalent fail-open predicates, disabled RLS, lost grants or missing workbench idempotency uniqueness may not be caught.
findings.fix: Assert relrowsecurity, exact normalized policy predicates, grants and all created indexes; add role-switched four-state visibility probes.

findings.evidence: Rollback intentionally restores NULL-permissive policies and drops NOT NULL.
findings.impact: Emergency rollback returns known tenant-isolation vulnerabilities; safety depends solely on the destructive gate and rapid re-apply.
findings.fix: Record the risk in runtime state and consider a safer fail-closed rollback mode requiring explicit choice.

findings.evidence: Resource reservation reservation_id and route-cost full logical key are not compounded with org_id while their tables are otherwise tenant isolated.
findings.impact: Cross-tenant ID/key reuse can produce uniqueness failures even though neither tenant can see the conflicting row.
findings.fix: Include org_id in remaining tenant-local business keys or document a global ID authority and enforce it.

semantic_analysis.migration_safety: Conditional idempotent DDL plus bounded data backfill executes in one transaction; replay on already-clean data is mostly no-op.
semantic_analysis.replay_safety: Fresh-chain replay is safe, but rollback intentionally reverses the security hardening.
semantic_analysis.owner_runtime_roles: Targets service_role and authenticated roles; function creation in public is intentional for standalone schema.
semantic_analysis.schema_alignment: Matches the current NOT NULL/composite mappings for covered tables; text visibility overload supports varchar trace spans.
semantic_analysis.injection_risk: Table names are a static array and default org is quoted via parameterized format %L.
semantic_analysis.verification_guarantees: Stronger structural assurance than 025 but still no behavioral isolation probe.

writes: enables RLS and replaces FOR ALL policies on execution, conflict, KPI, route cost matrix and policy activation
contracts: five previously unprotected org tables get RLS
tenant_boundaries: org_id text equality filters/writes by GUC
NULL fallback remains even though columns were made NOT NULL by 057
failure_paths: no grants are added here; relies on earlier table grants

findings.evidence: It claims alignment with 057 but adds `OR org_id IS NULL`, which 057 deliberately removed; direct replay after 057 reinstates that branch on five tables.
findings.impact: The fail-closed tenant contract is weakened; if a constraint rollback or future write makes NULL rows possible they become globally visible/writable.
findings.fix: Remove the NULL branches and align with the 057 global-admin/fail-closed shape; prevent replay of the obsolete policy body.

findings.evidence: Verification counts RLS flags and policies with service_role but never inspects policy USING/WITH CHECK expressions or behavior.
findings.impact: The NULL-permissive regression and many other fail-open policy bodies pass verification as long as names/roles are correct.
findings.fix: Assert normalized predicates and run role-switched org-A/org-B/no-GUC/write probes.

findings.evidence: The migration adds no grants and its verify does not check service_role privileges.
findings.impact: A fresh/partial database can pass policy structure checks while runtime DML fails, or privilege drift can go unnoticed.
findings.fix: GRANT the intended DML explicitly and verify has_table_privilege for each table.

semantic_analysis.migration_safety: DROP/CREATE and RLS enable are idempotent and transactional.
semantic_analysis.replay_safety: Direct replay is not forward-safe relative to 057 because it restores older fail-open expressions.
semantic_analysis.owner_runtime_roles: service_role is intended runtime; table owner bypass is used for retention.
semantic_analysis.schema_alignment: Matches org columns but not the final 057 policy contract.
semantic_analysis.injection_risk: Static DDL and validated schema token.
semantic_analysis.verification_guarantees: Only structural count/existence; no tenant isolation behavior is actually guaranteed by this verify.

writes: enables RLS and creates policies on resource locks, policy replay and replication sessions

default org fallback for factory replication
rollback must disable RLS with policy removal
tenant_boundaries: resource locks and policy replay are tenant scoped

findings.evidence: Existing NULL replication rows and the no-org fallback use lexicographic minimum or hardcoded sentinel.
findings.impact: Legacy cross-factory/global rows can be assigned to an arbitrary tenant; later visibility and cleanup become tenant-dependent.
findings.fix: Use an explicit approved org mapping/default or quarantine ambiguous rows before enabling RLS.

findings.evidence: The column is backfilled and given a default but is not altered to NOT NULL.
findings.impact: Owner/system paths inserting explicit NULL can still create rows invisible to every non-admin runtime context.
findings.fix: SET NOT NULL after backfill and reject explicit NULL, or create a separate global flow table.

findings.evidence: Behavioral probes cover SELECT visibility in four states but do not test INSERT/UPDATE WITH CHECK or grants.
findings.impact: A policy that reads correctly but accepts cross-tenant writes, or missing DML privileges, is not fully excluded by verify.
findings.fix: Add cross-tenant write rejection, self-org write success and privilege assertions.

findings.evidence: The DB-only column default is not represented in schema.ts orgId.
findings.impact: Schema introspection/push reports drift and ORM users may not understand fallback semantics.
findings.fix: Mirror the SQL default in Drizzle or prohibit push and generate an alignment receipt.

semantic_analysis.migration_safety: Idempotent data backfill, default change, RLS enable and policy replacement run in one transaction.
semantic_analysis.replay_safety: Forward-safe within its own scope; rollback correctly disables RLS and removes the default, preserving backfilled data.
semantic_analysis.owner_runtime_roles: Policy explicitly targets service_role and relies on ewoh_api NOBYPASSRLS membership for meaningful enforcement.
semantic_analysis.schema_alignment: Resource locks/policy replay align; factory replication default/NULL status drifts from Drizzle.
semantic_analysis.injection_risk: Static table names and parameter-safe format/default expressions.
semantic_analysis.verification_guarantees: Best in batch for read isolation: structural checks plus real role-switched org-A/org-B/no-GUC/admin SELECT probes; write-side guarantee is incomplete.

findings.evidence: Verification inspects catalog counts and policy text but never switches role or compares org-A/org-B visibility.
findings.impact: Semantically wrong policy bodies, missing grants or actual cross-tenant leakage can pass if names and substrings exist.
findings.fix: Add ewoh_api role-switched read/write probes and normalized policy predicate assertions.

findings.evidence: It only requires app.current_org_id to occur in qual or with_check, not in both normalized USING and WITH CHECK.
findings.impact: A write policy without tenant filtering can pass while the read policy contains the expected string.
findings.fix: Assert exact normalized predicates on both qual and with_check.

findings.evidence: The comment says runner uses >= counts for RLS/policies/GUC.
findings.impact: Structural duplication/extras are less likely due fixed names, but exact-state intent is weakened.
findings.fix: Return and assert exact cardinalities at the runner boundary.

semantic_analysis.verification_scope: Catalog/structure and textual GUC presence only.

semantic_analysis.owner_runtime_roles: No role switch, so owner/BYPASSRLS behavior is not exercised.

semantic_analysis.actual_guarantee: Proves objects/named policies exist and mention current_org_id somewhere; does not prove org isolation.

contracts: no literal org_id IS NULL branch

findings.evidence: The script validates named policies but never checks pg_class.relrowsecurity for scheduler/route or workbench tables.
findings.impact: Policies can remain as dormant metadata after RLS is disabled and verification still reports success, giving no DB isolation.
findings.fix: Assert relrowsecurity=true for every table intended to be protected.

findings.evidence: Checks only that literal `org_id IS NULL` is absent and roles contain service_role; does not normalize/exact policy predicates, check extra roles, grants, workbench relrowsecurity or uq_workbench_export_tasks_org_idem.
findings.impact: Equivalent fail-open expressions, extra policy roles, disabled RLS, privilege drift and a missing idempotency key can escape verification.
findings.fix: Assert exact normalized roles/predicates, RLS flags, grants and every created index; add behavioral probes.

findings.evidence: Unlike standalone_098, no role switch/GUC row visibility probe is performed.
findings.impact: Actual tenant isolation is not demonstrated end-to-end; only current catalog shape is inferred.
findings.fix: Run ewoh_api org-A/org-B/no-GUC/global-admin and write rejection probes.

semantic_analysis.verification_scope: Much broader structural coverage than 025 but still non-behavioral.
semantic_analysis.replay_safety: Read-only and safe to rerun aside from search_path.
semantic_analysis.owner_runtime_roles: No role switch; current connection bypasses RLS if owner/BYPASSRLS.
semantic_analysis.schema_alignment: Good coverage of NOT NULL/composite keys covered by migration, with known idempotency-index omission.
semantic_analysis.actual_guarantee: Proves selected policy/index/function structures exist, not that RLS is active or tenant-safe at runtime.

security_boundaries: policy role array must equal service_role
tenant_boundaries: policy predicates and actual row isolation are not inspected
failure_paths: structural count mismatch raises; marker is then absent and runner fails
tests: standalone chain verify and runner command

findings.evidence: Verification checks policy names and roles but not USING/WITH CHECK predicates.
findings.impact: The migration’s fail-open NULL branch, a bare true policy, or another cross-tenant predicate passes verification.
findings.fix: Assert exact normalized tenant predicates and absence of NULL/global fallback unless explicitly intended.

findings.evidence: No role switch, GUC setup or org-A/org-B visibility/write test exists.
findings.impact: RLS may still be ineffective due to role ownership, GUC wiring or predicate logic while structural checks pass.
findings.fix: Run behavioral read and write probes as in standalone_098.

findings.evidence: Service_role privileges are not asserted.
findings.impact: Policy shape can pass while runtime queries fail from missing DML grants; privilege drift is invisible.
findings.fix: Check has_table_privilege for intended SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE.

semantic_analysis.schema_alignment: Expected table set matches migration exactly.
semantic_analysis.actual_guarantee: Only proves objects and role scope; does not prove org predicates or isolation.

writes: inserts and deletes prefixed probe rows inside the DO block
switches to ewoh_api and sets GUCs

contracts: policy text contains current org and admin exception and is not bare true

findings.evidence: Behavioral coverage is SELECT-only; it does not attempt cross-tenant INSERT/UPDATE or test grants.
findings.impact: A policy with correct USING but permissive/missing WITH CHECK, or missing privileges, is not fully verified.
findings.fix: Add successful same-org writes and rejected cross-org writes/reads under ewoh_api plus has_table_privilege assertions.

findings.evidence: It does not assert replication_sessions.org_id nullability/default, even though policy relies on no NULL rows.
findings.impact: A rollback/constraint drift that permits explicit NULL can recreate invisible owner-inserted rows without failing verify.
findings.fix: Assert column nullability/default and reject explicit NULL in a probe.

findings.evidence: Cleanup uses broad `LIKE verify-098-%` prefixes and inserts real rows.
findings.impact: Collisions are unlikely but possible, and triggers/sequence side effects can occur; atomic DO block limits crash residue.
findings.fix: Use sufficiently namespaced UUID probes and document/verify no trigger side effects.

semantic_analysis.replay_safety: Probe rows are deleted on success/error; DO block is atomic, though verify itself is not wrapped as a runner transaction.

entry_points: DatabaseOrgHierarchyProvider used when Drizzle DB is injected
database_tables: ewoh_organization indirectly through org lookup functions
contracts: resolve root plus descendants by BFS
explicit invalidate per org/subtree or all
DatabaseOrgHierarchyProvider accepts org_id or row id conventions
security_boundaries: database functions parameterized through Drizzle sql
tenant_boundaries: organization scope determines descendant orgIds and inherited config
default provider silently trusts any requested org if no DB/provider is injected
multi-instance cache is eventually consistent up to TTL
failure_paths: cycle in loadEffectiveConfig returns empty parent config/ancestors without explicit cycle error

findings.evidence: Both DB and provider are optional; without DB the DEFAULT_PROVIDER accepts any org as existing and returns no children/config.
findings.impact: A DI/config regression silently disables real hierarchy validation and can expand scope around an arbitrary caller-supplied tenant ID instead of failing startup/request.
findings.fix: Require DB or provider at construction, or make DEFAULT_PROVIDER throw a fail-closed configuration error.

findings.evidence: Cache is an unbounded Map and cached resolution objects are returned directly with cached mutated on the shared object.
findings.impact: Many org IDs can grow memory indefinitely, and a caller mutating the returned resolution poisons future cached results.
findings.fix: Freeze/clone returned values and add bounded LRU/size control.

findings.evidence: The built-in DatabaseOrgHierarchyProvider does not implement optional loadAll, so it always uses recursive loadChildren queries.
findings.impact: Deep/wide organization trees cause N+1 database round trips despite the documented optimization path.
findings.fix: Implement a bounded loadAll query with tenant-safe predicates or remove/condition the optimization claim.

findings.evidence: A cycle returns empty config and ancestor IDs at the repeated node instead of raising a hierarchy error.
findings.impact: Corrupt organization graphs can produce misleading inherited configuration and incomplete invalidation semantics.
findings.fix: Detect and raise a cycle error, or define/validate explicit cycle behavior.

semantic_analysis.runtime_shape: Stateful Nest service with process-local cache; no events beyond local callbacks.
semantic_analysis.owner_runtime_roles: Database identity/GUC comes from the injected Drizzle connection; service itself does not set role or GUC.
semantic_analysis.org_isolation: It computes scope only; DB RLS must independently enforce row access. Parameterized DB functions prevent SQL injection.
semantic_analysis.schema_alignment: Matches organization dual id/org_id convention described in schema, but does not implement loadAll.
semantic_analysis.verification_guarantees: Unit tests cover provided-provider hierarchy/cache and DB child traversal, not missing-dependency fail-closed behavior, mutation safety or loadAll performance.
